system_overview: This specification models the Atomic Commitment Protocol with Simple Broadcast (ACP-SB), a distributed transaction commitment protocol from Babaoglu and Toueg's work on non-blocking atomic commitment. The protocol coordinates a group of participants and a coordinator to agree on committing or aborting a distributed transaction. The simple broadcast variant sends messages sequentially, which means a coordinator failure during broadcast can leave some participants without a decision, making it a blocking protocol that does not guarantee termination under failures.
actors_and_components: The system consists of two types of actors: (1) A single coordinator that collects votes from participants, makes a commit or abort decision, and broadcasts the decision. (2) A set of participants, each of which votes yes or no on the transaction, can detect failures, and ultimately reaches a commit or abort decision. Both the coordinator and participants can crash (die) at any time.
state_variables: The system tracks the following state: For each participant: their vote (yes or no), whether they are alive, their final decision (undecided, commit, or abort), whether they are faulty (have crashed), and whether they have sent their vote to the coordinator. For the coordinator: whether it has sent a vote request to each participant, the vote received from each participant (or a waiting indicator if not yet received), whether it has broadcast its decision to each participant (or a not-sent indicator), its own decision (commit, abort, or undecided), whether it is alive, and whether it is faulty.
initial_state: All participants start alive and non-faulty, each with a nondeterministically chosen vote of yes or no, undecided about the final outcome, and having not yet sent their vote. The coordinator starts alive and non-faulty, has not sent vote requests to any participant, has not received any votes (all waiting), has not broadcast any decision (all not-sent), and is undecided.
actions: The coordinator actions are: (1) Send a vote request to a participant (if the coordinator is alive and has not already requested from that participant). (2) Receive a vote from a participant (if the coordinator is alive, undecided, has requested all votes, is waiting on that participant, and the participant has sent its vote). (3) Detect a participant fault (if the coordinator is alive, undecided, has requested all votes, is waiting on that participant, and the participant has died without sending its vote -- the coordinator then decides to abort). (4) Make a decision (if the coordinator is alive, undecided, and has received all votes -- if all votes are yes, decide commit; otherwise, decide abort). (5) Broadcast the decision to a participant using simple broadcast (if the coordinator is alive, has made a decision, and has not yet sent it to that participant). (6) Die (the coordinator crashes and becomes faulty). The participant actions are: (1) Send vote (if the participant is alive and has received a vote request). (2) Abort on vote (if the participant is alive, undecided, has sent its vote, and its vote is no -- it decides unilaterally to abort). (3) Abort on timeout for vote request (if the participant is alive, undecided, and the coordinator has died without sending a vote request). (4) Decide based on coordinator broadcast (if the participant is alive, undecided, and the coordinator has sent a decision to it -- the participant adopts that decision). (5) Die (the participant crashes and becomes faulty).
safety_properties: AC1 (Agreement/Consistency): No two participants can decide differently -- it is impossible for one participant to have committed while another has aborted. AC2 (Commit validity): If any participant decides commit, then all participants must have voted yes. AC3 (Abort validity): If any participant decides abort, then either at least one participant voted no, or at least one participant is faulty, or the coordinator is faulty. AC4 (Irrevocability): Each participant decides at most once -- once a participant decides commit, it remains committed forever; once it decides abort, it remains aborted forever.
liveness_properties: AC3 liveness component: Eventually either all participants reach a decision (commit or abort), or at least one participant is faulty, or the coordinator is faulty. Note: The simple broadcast variant does NOT satisfy the non-blocking termination property AC5 (which would require that every non-faulty participant eventually decides). This is because a coordinator crash during broadcast can leave some participants permanently undecided.
model_bounds: The set of participants is declared as a constant. For model checking, safety was checked with up to 4 participants (without symmetries) and 6 participants (with symmetries). Liveness was checked for up to 4 participants.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on participant progress actions and coordinator progress actions, excluding death transitions -- that is, if a participant or the coordinator is able to make progress (send votes, make decisions, etc.), it eventually does. Death transitions are not subject to fairness and can occur at any time. The specification uses asynchronous communication rather than synchronous communication, and failure detection is modeled as immediate (magical) rather than timeout-based.
